key_insight: Bidirectional cross-modal prompting lets event and frame streams actively modulate each other’s representations, closing the modality gap so asymmetric event-frame stereo produces more reliable 3D perception under fast motion and challenging illumination.
problem_solved: Integrates high-temporal-resolution event data with rich-context frame images for asymmetric stereo while overcoming the modality gap that normally causes one modality to be marginalized, leading to poor depth estimation in dynamic or low-light scenes.
method: Design lightweight bidirectional prompts that carry complementary cues between an event encoder and a frame encoder to align and enrich features.
Use cross-modal prompting layers to iteratively refine per-modality representations before fusion, preserving modality-specific strengths (temporal detail from events, context from frames).
Fuse the prompted features in a stereo/geometry-aware decoder to produce robust disparity/depth estimates under motion and illumination challenges.
impact: Provides a practical way to combine event cameras with conventional cameras for more robust stereo/3D perception in robotics, autonomous vehicles, and computational photography without heavy architecture changes. Improves reliability in high-speed and low-light environments where traditional frame-only methods fail.

paper_title: Bidirectional Cross-Modal Prompting for Event-Frame Asymmetric Stereo
paper_authors: Ninghui Xu, Fabio Tosi, Lihui Wang, Jiawei Han, Luca Bartolomei
